info.name: Airborne Dashboard APIs
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for all Airborne Server dashboard APIs.

## Authentication
Most endpoints require a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Use the "Login" or "Issue Token" endpoints to obtain a token.

## Required Headers
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — for authenticated endpoints
- `x-organisation` — organisation name (for org-scoped endpoints)
- `x-application` — application name (for app-scoped endpoints)

---

## Path to Release (Step-by-Step)

Below is the full workflow to go from zero to a live release, with curl examples.

### Step 1: Register a user
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/users/create \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"myuser","password":"MyPass@123","email":"user@example.com"}'
```
Save the `access_token` from `user_token` in the response.

### Step 2: Create an organisation
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/organisations/create \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"my-org"}'
```

### Step 3: Create an application
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/organisations/applications/create \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"application":"my-app"}'
```

### Step 4: Create dimensions (optional, for targeting)
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/organisations/applications/dimension/create \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"dimension":"os","schema":"string","description":"Operating system","dimension_type":"standard","depends_on":null}'
```

### Step 5: Upload files
Upload the files that will be part of your release bundle.
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/file/upload?file_path=index.js \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -F 'file=@./dist/index.js'
```
Repeat for each file. Note the `file_path` values returned.

### Step 6: Create a package
Bundle the uploaded files into a package. The `index` field is the entry-point file path, `files` lists all file paths.
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/packages \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"index":"index.js","tag":"v1.0.0","files":["index.js","style.css"]}'
```
Note the `package_key` (format: `index@version:N`) from the response headers or body.

### Step 7: Create a release
Reference a package by `package_id` (resolves against the application's **primary** package group). Both `package_id` and `package` are required. Use `sub_packages: ["<group_id>@<version>"]` to pull in additional non-primary groups.
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/releases \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "config": {
      "boot_timeout": 5000,
      "release_config_timeout": 3000,
      "properties": {}
    },
    "package_id": "index.js@version:1",
    "package": {
      "properties": {},
      "important": [],
      "lazy": []
    },
    "sub_packages": [],
    "dimensions": {"os": "android"},
    "resources": []
  }'
```
Save the `id` from the response — this is your `release_id`.

The configured validation function (see Validation Functions folder) is invoked on every Create Release; if it returns false the request is rejected.

### Step 8: Ramp the release (gradual rollout)
Increase traffic to the new release.
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/releases/<RELEASE_ID>/ramp \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"traffic_percentage": 50, "change_reason": "Canary rollout to 50%"}'
```

### Step 9: Conclude or discard
**Conclude** (promote to 100%):
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/releases/<RELEASE_ID>/conclude \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"chosen_variant": "control", "change_reason": "Metrics look good, rolling out"}'
```
**Discard** (rollback):
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/api/releases/<RELEASE_ID>/discard \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'x-organisation: my-org' \
  -H 'x-application: my-app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"change_reason": "Found regression, rolling back"}'
```

### Step 10: Serve the release (public, no auth)
Clients fetch the current release via:
```
curl http://localhost:8081/release/my-org/my-app
```
Or v2 with experiment toss:
```
curl http://localhost:8081/release/v2/my-org/my-app?toss=42
```

request.description:
Exchanges a Personal Access Token (PAT) for a short-lived OIDC access token.

Body is the JSON downloaded when the PAT was created via `POST /token`: `{ client_id, client_secret }`. Public endpoint — no Authorization header.

The test script auto-stores the returned `access_token` into the `{{access_token}}` collection variable so subsequent requests in this collection authenticate automatically.

Creates a Personal Access Token for the logged-in user. The `name` MUST equal the authenticated user's username (server checks `auth_response.username == req.name` and rejects with 401 Unauthorized otherwise). Set the `{{username}}` collection variable accordingly.

item.name: Package Groups
item.description: Package Groups are the v2 packaging model. Every application gets a `primary` group at creation time. The primary group requires `index` on each package and is what `package_id` resolves against in Create Release. Non-primary groups (sub-packages) must NOT supply `index` and are referenced from a release via `sub_packages: ["<group_id>@<version>"]`.

request.description: Creates a new non-primary package group. `is_primary` is always false here — the primary group is auto-created with the application.

request.description:
Creates a new v2 package version inside the group. Server auto-assigns `version = max(existing) + 1` scoped to the group.

• Primary group: `index` is REQUIRED and must reference an existing file (e.g. add `"index": "index.js@version:1"` to the body).
• Non-primary group: `index` MUST be omitted/null — the request fails otherwise.

The default example body omits `index` because the `Create Package Group` request creates non-primary groups. Add `index` only when targeting the auto-created `primary` group.

All entries in `files` are resolved by `<file_path>@version:N` or `<file_path>@tag:NAME`; missing files reject the request.
